the QTL for seed weight were different at each stage of development and the seed weight QTL were affected by QTL x environment interactions.
QTL underlying the seed weight during the seed development of soybean were detected and that QTL × environment interaction effects were identified.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of QTL underlying seed weight and the analysis of QE interaction effects on mean seed weight.
the identification of QTL underlying soybean seed size during development.
the development of a genetic map for soybean and with the identification and location of QTL affecting mean seed weight at six different development stages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genetic effects and the number of QTL affecting the mean seed weight were different at each development stage.

QTL underlying seed weight are dynamic during seed development and that QE interactions are significant in soybean seed development and that the genetic effects of QTL underlying seed traits are dynamic during seed growth.
the genetic architecture for seed weight during development was complex and highly dynamic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the seed weight is the sum of development of seeds and the response to stress during seed development.

seed weight was affected by QTL with different main effects and QTL × Environment interaction effects at different developmental stages and that the QTL × Environment effects were important for the final seed weight at harvest.
seed weight is a quantitative trait with many QTL and the expression of these QTL varies during seed development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic control of seed weight during development is complex.
the genetic architecture of the soybean seed weight trait is complex, with a number of QTL affecting the trait at different developmental stages, and the QTL effects are different at each stage.
the genetic effects on the mean seed weight are different at the different developmental stages, but the QTL are stable across the environments.
